fixes.explanation: Not boats, baker. The text says she set the basket “…among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.” (Exodus 2:3) Boats don't come up in this verse at all. The reeds are the only neighbors the basket gets.

Yes, baker. The text says his sister “…stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.” (Exodus 2:4) She was watching, and that's the reason the verse gives. I think she watched that basket like I watch the oven timer.
You got it, baker. She said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) That's what she called him. And the verse says she had compassion on him.
Not Egyptian, friend. She said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) Hebrew is the word she used for him. The verse also says she had compassion on him.
Yes, baker. The text says “…the girl went and called the boy’s mother.” (Exodus 2:8) Out of every woman she could have called, she called his own mother. I think that's a plot twist worth a gasp.
Not the desert, friend. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.” (Exodus 2:10) The word she gave was water. Desert isn't in her explanation.
Not mountains, baker. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.” (Exodus 2:10) Water is the word in her explanation. Mountains aren't in it.
